title: the sudo relay's local executor runs its command under the host's bash, not WSL's
intention: relay.local_executor spawns shutil.which('bash') on Windows, so its command runs in the box's own shell and sees Windows paths intact.
why: Measured 2026-11-12 on akiendell: relay.local_executor('echo hi; uname -a; pwd; echo C:\\Users\\x') on akiendell returned Linux ... WSL2, /mnt/c/automation/local/cairn and C:Usersx
traces_to: Law 3: a spawn is not known to run the intended shell until measured; Law 4: enforced by a scan, not remembered.
how: In cairn/devices/sudo_relay/relay.py add a private _bash() returning shutil.which('bash') or 'bash' where os.name is nt, else 'bash'; local_executor uses it. root_executor is unchanged (sudo does not exist on Windows). The red-first proof stubs _run to capture argv and asserts argv[0], plus an AST scan of relay.py that no list literal begins with the bare string bash outside _bash.

clauses.claim: on nt, local_executor hands _run an argv whose first element is shutil.which('bash'), where it was the bare word bash
an AST scan of relay.py finds no list literal starting with the bare string bash outside _bash

decisions.text: D2: one proof, one tooth per clause; red first.
